prompt.value:
Mutability of lists
What is the output of the following snippet of code?

P = [1, 2, 3]
Q = P
P.append(4)
print(P)
print(Q)

explanation.value:
In line-2, we are not creating a new object. We are merely creating another name, also called an
alias, for the same object. Think of this like having a nickname. Your name and nickname are two different words,
but both of them refer to you. To see if two Python names point to the same object, we can use the keyword:
print(P is Q) This will print the value . This means that and are two different names for the same underlying list
object. For a more detailed treatment of mutability, refer the .
